title: Cohomology of punctured generalization neighborhoods as a filtered colimit
statement: Let $T$ be a spectral topological space [def-weil-spectral-space], let $Z\subseteq T$ be closed with quasi-compact open complement $U=T\setminus Z$, and let $A$ be a sheaf of abelian groups on $T$. Set $W=\{t\in T:\overline{\{t\}}\cap Z\ne\varnothing\}$ and $S=W\setminus Z$, with their subspace topologies. For a subspace $B\subseteq T$, write $A|_B$ for the inverse image along its inclusion [def-weil-pbc-topological-inverse-image]. For every integer $p\geq0$ the canonical restriction maps induce an isomorphism of abelian groups $$\varinjlim_{Z\subseteq N\subseteq T,\ N\text{ quasi-compact open}} H^p(N\setminus Z,A|_{N\setminus Z})\ \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\ H^p(S,A|_S).$$ Here cohomology is the right-derived global sections of abelian sheaves [def-sc-topological-abelian-cohomology], and the colimit [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] is over the set of quasi-compact open neighborhoods $N$ of $Z$, ordered by reverse inclusion, with restriction transition maps. This index set is nonempty (it contains $T$) and directed (intersections are quasi-compact open).

source.place: Tag 0A3D, label lemma-cohomology-of-neighbourhoods-of-closed, part (2), specialized to a closed subset whose open complement is quasi-compact; such Z is constructible and quasi-compact in a spectral space

proof.text: The index of compact open neighborhoods, ordered by reverse inclusion, is nonempty since it contains the whole spectral space. Intersecting two neighborhoods gives a common later stage because compact opens in a spectral space are closed under intersection. The index is a preorder category, so parallel morphisms are equal. This proves the asserted IsFiltered instance.

For injectivity of the canonical colimit comparison, represent a colimit element z at some neighborhood N, using preservation of filtered colimits by the forgetful functor on abelian groups. If the comparison kills z, the canonical cocone leg kills its representative x. Apply punctured-neighborhood eventual vanishing to obtain a later neighborhood M on which x restricts to zero. The defining colimit relation identifies z with the image of that zero class, hence z is zero. An additive homomorphism with trivial kernel is injective.

For surjectivity, the punctured-neighborhood class-lifting theorem represents every target class by a class x at a neighborhood N. The image of x under the N-th colimit coprojection maps to the desired target class by the colimit.desc coprojection equation. The comparison is therefore bijective, hence an isomorphism in AddCommGrpCat. Both halves concern the specified canonical cocone, so the proof proves invertibility of the canonical comparison.

proof_origin.place: Tag 0A3D(2), canonical comparison proved from its class-lifting and eventual-vanishing halves
